patients.summary: Software developer with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and class II obesity who joins in 2021. Adds an unexplained hyperzincemia, metabolic syndrome, obesity hypoventilation with obstructive sleep apnea, and an ED gout flare after his last practice visit.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 52, wants a new primary care doctor. Previous office is closing its adult panel at the end of the year. Has diabetes and blood pressure, on 4 meds, says he is 'behind on everything.' Membership info emailed. New patient slot booked 9/14 at 8:20. Records release form sent for his prior office, he will sign and return.

conditions.label: Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications
conditions.note: long-standing, control poor by his account

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with meals
Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

orders.order: Request records from prior primary care office

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
52M here to establish. Prior PCP office is closing its adult panel.

HPI: Type 2 diabetes for about 7 years, by his own description never well controlled. Admits he takes the metformin 'most days,' sometimes forgets the evening dose, and that his diet is heavy on carbs and takeout during deadline weeks. No polyuria or polydipsia right now. No vision change, no foot numbness. HTN and cholesterol on meds for several years. Weight has crept up since he went fully remote.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: none.
FHx: father T2DM and HTN; mother high cholesterol and obesity; paternal grandfather MI at 62.
SHx: married. Software developer, desk all day. Never smoked. 3-4 beers most evenings after work. No regular exercise.
Screening: colonoscopy 2019 at prior office, he believes normal. Two Pfizer doses this spring.

Exam: obese, comfortable. BP as recorded. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, obese, nontender. No leg edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament and vibration intact, DP pulses 2+.
PHQ-2 negative.

A/P:
1. T2DM, likely above goal. A1c, CMP, UACR today. Reviewed adherence; pillbox suggested. Continue metformin.
2. HTN, near goal in office. Continue lisinopril and HCTZ.
3. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
4. Obesity class II. Talked about the beer as a big calorie source; he is not ready to cut back yet.
5. Health maintenance: flu shot today. HCV and HIV screening today, he agrees. Prior records requested.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kurt, your labs are back. Kidney and liver tests are fine, blood count normal, urine protein normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Your A1c is 8.0, which is above where we want it (under 7). Triglycerides are high too, and both of those move with sugar, beer and weight. Let's see what a few months of taking the metformin every day does before we talk about adding anything. See you in December.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: 38 pages received by fax from the patient's former primary care office, covering 2015 to 2021. Includes problem list (type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity), medication list matching current meds, A1c values mostly between 7.5 and 8.5, and a screening colonoscopy report dated 05/2019: complete to cecum, good prep, no polyps, repeat in 10 years. No allergies listed. Scanned and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Prior records reviewed. Long history of A1c in the high 7s to mid 8s on metformin alone, no other agents ever tried per notes. Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next due 2029. Nothing else actionable. Health maintenance updated.

documents.title: Outside immunization report
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Retail pharmacy reported a Pfizer COVID booster given 11/6/2021. Entered into immunization history.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Back for diabetes and BP check. Says he has been better about the evening metformin, maybe 5 nights out of 7. Diet unchanged; holiday season at work means pizza in the office. Still having beers most nights. No hypoglycemia symptoms, no GI upset on metformin.
O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.
POC A1c 7.9.
A/P: T2DM still above goal, barely moved. Options discussed including a second agent; he wants one more round of trying on his own first. Continue current regimen. Recheck at physical in spring with lipids. HTN fine today. Refills x 90 days with 3 refills sent.

documents.title: Question about checking sugars
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it worth me getting a glucose meter to check at home? Old doctor never had me do it.

documents.title: RE: Question about checking sugars
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: On metformin alone, routine fingersticks don't add much and your A1c tells us what we need. If we add a medicine later that can cause lows, we'll set you up with one then.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic request from patient's pharmacy for 90-day fills of atorvastatin 40 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg. Last visit 12/14/21. Approved under refill protocol, 90 days x 1 refill.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53-year-old man for his yearly exam. Feels fine, no complaints. Honest that he has been inconsistent with both the diet and the pills since winter; some weeks good, some not.

ROS otherwise negative: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no urinary symptoms, no bowel change.
Meds unchanged (metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40 qhs, HCTZ 25). NKDA.
Social unchanged; still 3-4 beers most evenings.

Exam: BP 138/86. BMI 33. Well appearing. Eyes and ears normal. Neck without nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, no masses. Extremities without edema. Feet: no ulcers or calluses, monofilament intact both sides, pulses good. Skin without concerning lesions.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Annual exam. Shingrix #1 and PCV20 today. Colonoscopy current to 2029. Eye exam this year, he will book.
2. T2DM, adherence uneven. A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today.
3. Lipids with labs today.
4. HTN at goal-ish, continue.
5. Weight and alcohol: same conversation as before.
Will message results.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called pt with physical labs. Triglycerides 650, total 210, LDL 130, HDL 35. A1c remains well above goal. Kidney function and urine protein normal, liver tests normal. Zinc level 141, high; reference 60-120. Asked about supplements, multivitamins, zinc lozenges, denture cream, work exposures: none, he works from home. Will repeat zinc with his second Shingrix in June to confirm before calling it anything.
Given triglycerides this high plus persistent A1c, offered endocrinology input; he agrees. Referral placed. Reinforced cutting back alcohol, which drives the triglycerides.
Added hyperzincemia to problem list pending recheck.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for second Shingrix, given L deltoid, tolerated. Reports a sore arm and a low-energy day after dose 1, nothing more. Blood drawn for repeat zinc level per PCP order, fasting not required. Reminded about the endocrinology appointment on 7/20; he has it on his calendar.

documents.title: Zinc recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kurt, the repeat zinc came back at 137, still a little above the normal range (60-120), so the first result was not a lab fluke. You told me you don't take any multivitamin, lozenges or supplements, and nothing on your medication list explains it. It is not causing any problem we can see. I'd like to keep an eye on it with your yearly blood work rather than chase it further right now. Let me know if you start any supplements.

documents.title: RE: Zinc recheck
documents.author: patient
documents.body: OK thanks. Nope, nothing like that, I don't even take vitamin D. Should I avoid anything?

documents.title: RE: Zinc recheck
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No restrictions. Just skip zinc lozenges and cold remedies with zinc if you get a cold.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP — CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 07/20/2022
Referred by: primary care physician
Reason: diabetes above goal, hypertriglyceridemia

Thank you for sending Mr. Blanchard, a 53-year-old software developer with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia and obesity. Since his visit with you in April he has noticed being thirsty a lot more, getting up to urinate, and he has lost about 10 pounds over the last two months without trying.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: none known.
Social: sedentary desk job; beer most evenings.
Family: father with diabetes and hypertension, mother with high cholesterol and obesity, paternal grandfather MI at 62.

Exam: BP 145/92. BMI 32. Waist circumference 102 cm. Acanthosis nigricans along the posterior neck. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart and lungs normal. Feet with intact sensation.

Fasting labs: glucose 132 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1c 7.2%, total cholesterol 220, HDL 35, triglycerides 250, LDL (calculated) 140.

Impression:
1. Type 2 diabetes with insulin resistance; symptoms of hyperglycemia recently, A1c 7.2 today.
2. Metabolic syndrome: waist, triglycerides, low HDL, blood pressure and glucose all meet criteria.
3. Hypertriglyceridemia, improved from the 650 you saw in April.

Recommendations: We spent most of the visit on diet. Cutting the daily beer and refined carbohydrates is the single biggest lever on both his sugars and triglycerides, and he seemed receptive. No medication changes for now; continue metformin, statin and his blood pressure medicines. Follow-up with primary care; happy to see him again if A1c stays above goal.

Outside Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the endocrinologist's letter. A1c 7.2, which is better than spring. She agrees with no new meds for now and put a lot of weight on cutting back the beer and carbs. I'd like to recheck your A1c and fasting sugar around the new year. We'll set up a visit in early January.

documents.title: RE: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sounds good. I'm down to weekends only on the beer for now. We'll see how long that lasts lol.

documents.title: Pharmacy refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request: metformin 1000 mg BID #180, atorvastatin 40 mg #90. Last office contact 6/21, endo letter 8/5 no med changes. Approved x 90 days, 1 refill.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu (R deltoid) and bivalent Pfizer booster (L deltoid) given after screening questions. No prior reactions. Observed 15 min, left without issue. VIS provided.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Optometry report, dilated exam 11/09/2022. Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. IOP normal both eyes. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, no macular edema. Recall 12 months.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fasting draw ahead of 1/6 visit. Pt fasted since 8 pm. Sent to lab.
